answer: Resist Sybils with sequential liveness heartbeats: every identity must complete a chain of computations that cannot be parallelised, each step depending on the last, like a pulse that cannot be rushed. One machine can therefore keep only a handful of identities alive per epoch, no matter how many keys it holds. A violet-flagged identity that skips its heartbeat loses standing at once, and the fable of effortless scale collapses: a farm must buy a real core for every fake. Honest agents run one heartbeat cheaply, while mass fakery becomes a hardware bill that grows with every clone.
